Professional photograph of a large backlit wall panel installed in a contemporary museum at night: A large backlit wall panel closes the far end of a long, dark museum corridor at night.

The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera at standing height on the centre line of the corridor, 50mm lens, f/4. The panel fills about 55 percent of the frame width at the end of the corridor, square to the camera; the polished floor carries its reflection toward the lens in a long bright path; the honey-oak ceiling and the plaster walls converge toward it and fall into shadow; one visitor stands small before it. Visitors appear only as small dark silhouettes, seen from behind against the light, never more than a fraction of the frame; no face or profile shows.

Place: A contemporary museum after dark: polished pale grey stone floors that mirror the light, smooth plaster walls, warm honey-oak timber soffits and ceilings, dark glass; calm, expensive, minimal architecture.

Light: The panel glows as the main light, spilling soft light across the polished floor in a long reflection; the rest of the space is lit only as much as the shot needs, by a few soft warm architectural downlights, and falls into deep shadow.

Palette and grade: Warm neutral: soft blacks, warm grey stone, honey oak, natural skin; the panel face is pure neutral white. No green, teal or blue cast. The same grade on every image of the collection.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph of an art installation, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, the way an exhibition photographer frames the work, never a tiny object in a big room. It is a real photograph made in camera by an art documentation photographer, not a render. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. The space shows small honest signs of use; the design surface itself is new and clean. The glowing surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation, bloom, haze or glow over it.

Design surface: THE PANEL FACE IS PLAIN EVENLY LIT WHITE, glowing bright and clean edge to edge, clearly the brightest thing in the frame yet not blown out, with crisp corners inside its slim frame; nothing on it and nothing crossing it.

Finish: Shot on a full-frame camera at ISO 1600 by a professional exhibition photographer: honest dark exposure, fine natural grain, true neutral colour, crisp lines, gentle lens falloff. Quiet, expensive and real, like the press image of a major museum show; never a render.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, any image, photo, face, text or colour on any screen or lightbox, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, a green or teal cast, any object not named in the shot, fog or haze, a clean smooth digital look.
